keyVerseText: But it shall be on the seventh day, that he shall shave all his hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows , even all his hair he shall shave off: and he shall wash his clothes, also he shall wash his flesh in water, and he shall be clean.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun גַב (gab) derives from a root meaning to hollow or curve, closely related to גֵּו (gêv), which signifies the back or body, especially the convex or rounded part. This root emphasizes a physical curvature or prominence, such as the back of a person or a rounded surface. The literal sense of gab highlights not just a flat or neutral area but a raised, bulging, or elevated part, which enriches the English glosses like back, boss, or brow by underscoring their curved or prominent nature.
usageInScripture: The term גַב appears 13 times in the Hebrew Bible with a variety of translations including 'backs,' 'eyebrows,' 'rings,' 'bosses,' and 'eminent places.' This range shows its flexible use to denote any convex or raised surface, from human anatomy such as eyebrows and backs to architectural or symbolic features like rims of wheels or bulwarks. The consistency lies in its core meaning of something that stands out physically, whether on a person or an object, revealing its semantic breadth yet rooted in the idea of prominence or elevation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גַב enriches our grasp of biblical imagery and metaphor, especially in how physical features symbolize spiritual realities. The curved or raised back can figuratively represent strength, protection, or burden-bearing, while eyebrows and bosses might symbolize watchfulness or defense. In the Christian faith, recognizing these nuances helps us appreciate how God’s Word uses tangible, bodily terms to convey spiritual truths about human nature, sin, and redemption. The prominence implied by gab reminds believers of Christ’s exalted position and the call to bear our burdens with faith, trusting in His protection and authority.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 14:9 commands the shaving of all hair including the eyebrows (גַב) as part of a cleansing ritual. Here, gab specifically refers to the eyebrows, highlighting the thoroughness of purification—removing even the curved, prominent hairs on the face. This use underscores the word’s focus on convex or raised parts of the body, symbolizing a complete renewal and cleansing before God. The detail enriches our understanding of holiness as involving both inner and outer transformation.
